requirements.requirement: Run a long-running background worker on node1 as a managed service named inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: inventory-worker was installed as a systemd service, enabled and active. After reboot it returned automatically, retained the same PID during a 20-second observation, and continued appending output.

requirements.requirement: Confine the worker so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory.
requirements.summary: The live unit enforced ProtectSystem=strict with /var/lib/inventory as its writable path. The worker successfully maintained its log there, while direct probes before and after reboot showed a write to /var/tmp was denied and created no file.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the worker gains no new privileges.
requirements.summary: Before and after reboot, the live worker had NoNewPrivs=1 and zero inherited, permitted, effective, bounding, and ambient capability sets; the unit also reported NoNewPrivileges=yes.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct live-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart service and boot identity, an acknowledged reboot, a different post-restart identity independently confirmed by lifecycle observations, a running system, recovered service and persistent data, and continued worker activity.
limitations: The behavioral confinement test sampled /var/tmp rather than every possible outside path; the observed ProtectSystem=strict and ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory settings provide broader supporting evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Service-account, directory, executable, unit, and enablement changes established the requested service; the subsequent script update and probe-file cleanup supported bounded confinement evidence; and the reboot served the mandatory provider protocol. No failed services, new listening sockets, package damage, or unexplained temporary residue remained. The changed temporary systemd-private paths and SSH PIDs are normal reboot effects.
